_comment: Does this app give its members a place to meet? It ships OFF, and off means absent: while this is false, /dashboard/community answers the same 404 a route that never existed answers — for everyone, the operator included. Switching on is this line plus the next deploy; there is no runtime toggle and no admin setting, deliberately, because the off state is the module's security kill-switch. Anything but true counts as off, and so does a broken file.
_comment_live: How often an open discussion asks what is new. visibleSeconds is what somebody looking at the page waits (bounded above by ten seconds — past that a conversation stops feeling like one) and hiddenSeconds is what a backgrounded tab waits, so a page left open overnight does not cost a host twelve requests a minute for a room nobody is reading. Same rules as the block above: an out-of-range value, a wrong type or an unknown key here switches the WHOLE COMMUNITY OFF until the next deploy, and the reason appears on /dashboard/community. hiddenSeconds shorter than visibleSeconds is refused rather than obeyed — that is the wrong way round.
_comment_posting: Writing a post: how often, and with how many pictures. maxPer10Min is a noise and cost brake, not a security control — it has to forgive somebody genuinely answering five people in a row. imagesMax is how many of their own pictures a member may attach to one post: three ships, ten is the hard ceiling, and 0 means this community is text — no upload field appears in the composer and the server refuses any picture. Set it to 0 if you would rather not store or moderate member-uploaded images at all; that is a product decision, not a misconfiguration. ⚠ A value outside those ranges, a wrong type, or an unknown key in this block does NOT quietly fall back — it makes the config incoherent, and an incoherent config switches the WHOLE COMMUNITY OFF until the next deploy. That is deliberate (the failure mode of this file is member data flowing where nobody decided it should), but it means editing these numbers carelessly is an outage rather than a no-op. The reason appears on /dashboard/community, which is the one page that stays reachable in that state.
_comment_messaging: The same brake for private messages, per member per ten minutes — its own bucket and deliberately tighter than the room's. A member answering five people in a discussion is a conversation; a member opening five private conversations in as many minutes is the shape unwanted contact takes. Same rules as the block above: an out-of-range value (1–200), a wrong type or an unknown key here switches the WHOLE COMMUNITY OFF until the next deploy, and the reason appears on /dashboard/community. This is a noise brake, not a safety control — what actually stops one member reaching another is the block, which the member sets themselves.
_comment_report: Spam-Meldungen. maxPer10Min ist die dritte Bremse des Moduls und darf grosszuegig bleiben — wer sechs Spam-Beitraege in zehn Minuten meldet, tut genau das, wofuer die Funktion da ist. attachmentMax ist etwas anderes und wichtiger: wie viele Nachrichten aus einem privaten Gespraech eine Meldung mitnehmen darf, damit ein Moderator den Zusammenhang sieht. Fuenf reichen fuer ein Muster und sind wenige genug, dass „der Moderator hat meine ganze Korrespondenz gelesen" nie stimmt; die harte Obergrenze ist zehn. Jeder unlesbare Wert faellt auf die VORGABE zurueck, nie auf „unbegrenzt" — und wird gemeldet, was wie ueberall hier die ganze Community bis zum naechsten Deploy abschaltet.
_comment_sendblock: Die automatische Sende-Sperre. Fuenf VERSCHIEDENE Meldende innerhalb von 24 Stunden legen das Schreiben eines Mitglieds still — lesen kann es weiterhin alles. Fuenf, damit eine einzelne veraergerte Person niemanden stilllegen kann; 24 Stunden, weil ein duennes Rinnsal von Beschwerden ueber ein Jahr eine Moderationsfrage ist und keine Spam-Welle. Ein Schwellwert von 1 wird NICHT befolgt (er waere ein Ein-Tipp-Knebel) und faellt auf die Vorgabe zurueck. expiryDays: null ist die Antwort auf OQ-4 — die Sperre steht, bis jemand sie aufhebt, denn v1 hat keinen Benachrichtigungskanal und ein stiller Ablauf entsperrt einen Spammer, ohne dass es jemand erfaehrt; das Aufheben ist EIN protokollierter Tipp in der Meldungs-Warteschlange. Betreiber und Moderatoren werden nie automatisch gesperrt — sonst uebernaehme die Community ihre eigene Moderation, wer sich am schnellsten organisiert. Es gibt KEINE Sperr-Tabelle: die Sperre wird aus den unbearbeiteten Meldungen abgeleitet, deshalb hebt sie sich selbst auf, wenn die aus dem Fenster laufen.
_comment_retention: How long private messages are kept. 0 — the shipped value — means: until the account that wrote them is deleted, and nothing prunes them by age. ⚠ Zero is the OFF sentinel here, which is the opposite of what it means in a cron retention window: every unreadable value in this field falls back to 0, so a typo KEEPS data instead of deleting it. A positive whole number (1–120 months) turns on bulk-by-age pruning. Two things trigger it and they differ in one way that matters: `node run.mjs community-prune` is a dry run unless you pass --apply, and the scheduled job `community-prune` (modules/community/cron.ts) cannot ask — it deletes. That job declares `enabledByDefault: false`, so nothing is deleted on a schedule until an operator ADDS an entry for it to config/cron.json with 'enabled': true — the entry is absent from the shipped file on purpose, because that file belongs to the core and may not name a job an app without this module does not have; setting a window in THIS field alone changes only what the command would do. There is deliberately no way to delete ONE conversation: choosing which means knowing what is in it, and that is read access by another name. Out-of-range or non-integer values switch the WHOLE COMMUNITY OFF until the next deploy, like every other field here.
